method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of the ASHM hepatitis C page. Thresholds, intervals and ages compared character by character. DAA regimens are not on the source page and are recorded as input_unavailable, NOT reconstructed from model memory. The source's use of 'positive SVR' to denote treatment failure, and the incomplete unit 'AST 40/L', are transcribed as written and flagged rather than reinterpreted. RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-22: the page in retrieved_from was fetched again and every claim attributed to this source was re-checked against it. Quotes stored from the earlier scrape carried that scrape's table and list markup (pipes, numbered list markers) into the quoted string; each was replaced with the text the page actually carries, located by alignment against the retrieved copy (scripts/repair_quotes.py). No dose, duration or concentration changed: the set of numbers in every repaired quote was compared before and after, and the only difference across 156 repaired quotes was list numerals 1-4 becoming bullets. Where a reference superscript falls inside a quoted sentence the page renders it inline, so it appears in source_text; it is part of the retrieved text, not part of the assertion.

claims.claim: Almost all patients can be successfully cured with direct-acting antiviral therapy
claims.source_text: Almost all patients can be successfully cured with direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy.

claims.claim: Current injecting drug use does not exclude a patient from treatment initiation
claims.source_text: Current injecting drug use Current injecting drug use does not exclude patient from treatment initiation

claims.claim: All HCV PCR positive patients should be given the opportunity to be treated
claims.source_text: All HCV PCR positive patients should be given the opportunity to be treated.

claims.claim: The auditable outcomes are that 100% of hepatitis C antibody positive patients have a hepatitis C RNA performed and 100% of antibody positive RNA positive patients are offered HCV treatment
claims.source_text: 100% of hepatitis C antibody positive patients have a hepatitis C RNA performed - 100% of hepatitis C antibody positive/RNA positive patients are offered HCV treatment

claims.claim: Re-infection should be treated again
claims.source_text: Re-infection Treat again

claims.claim: No dose adjustment is required for people over 65 years old
claims.source_text: Over 65 years old No dose adjustment required

claims.claim: Treatment advice and initiation should be in collaboration with HCV treatment providers until the clinician is comfortable with the decision-making process and prescribing
claims.source_text: Treatment advice and initiation in collaboration with HCV treatment providers until you are comfortable with the decision-making process and prescribing.

claims.claim: A detected hepatitis C antibody indicates past or current infection, while not detected indicates no evidence of infection
claims.source_text: Hepatitis C antibody (Hep C Ab) Detected: Infection with hepatitis C (past or current) Not detected: no evidence of infection

claims.claim: Detected HCV RNA indicates active infection, not detected indicates past or cleared infection or never infected, and it is used for test of cure or test of re-infection
claims.source_text: HCV RNA (NAAT)/HCV PCR Detected: active infection Not detected: past/cleared infection; never had infection NB: Use for test of cure or test of re-infection

claims.claim: Following successful treatment or natural clearance, HCV RNA will be negative although hepatitis C antibody will remain positive
claims.source_text: Following successful treatment or natural clearance of hepatitis C virus, HCV RNA will be negative although hepatitis C antibody will remain positive

claims.claim: Never repeat an HCV antibody test if initially positive
claims.source_text: Never repeat an HCV antibody test if initially positive.

claims.claim: Only use HCV PCR on patients with previous HCV infection, and HCV PCR is required for patients with previously cleared or treated infection who require ongoing testing
claims.source_text: Only use HCV PCR on patients with previous HCV infection ... HCV PCR is required for patients with previously cleared or treated infection who require ongoing testing.

claims.claim: Reflex testing is an HCV PCR done if an HCV antibody test is positive, allowing diagnosis without recalling the client; two EDTA samples need to be collected with the initial serum sample, and the local pathology service should be checked as sample preparation differs in metropolitan, regional and rural areas
claims.source_text: Reflex testing is an HCV PCR test done if an HCV antibody test is positive. The opportunity to diagnose HCV status is done without having to recall the client. Two EDTA samples need to be collected with the initial serum sample. Request HCV PCR if HCV antibody (anti-HCV) confirmed positive (ensure with the local pathology service if this test is possible, as sample preparation will differ in metropolitan, regional and rural areas).

claims.claim: A finger prick point-of-care HCV RNA test gives a result in 60 minutes and is useful for test and treat models of care
claims.source_text: Finger prick blood test HCV RNA Point-of-care test Result in 60 minutes - useful for test and treat models of care

claims.claim: Past cleared hepatitis C infection does not provide immunity against re-infection, and retesting is required if there is continued risk of re-exposure
claims.source_text: Past cleared hepatitis C infection does not provide immunity against re-infection. ... Clearance of hepatitis C does not provide immunity from re-infection. Retesting is required if there is a continued risk of re-exposure

claims.claim: If the patient has ongoing risk factors an annual HCV RNA test should be performed, and if re-infected offer re-treatment and harm reduction strategies
claims.source_text: If your patient has ongoing risk factors annual HCV RNA test. If re-infected offer re-treatment and harm reduction strategies

claims.claim: Ensure the patient uses new equipment if they continue to inject drugs
claims.source_text: Ensure your patient uses new equipment if they continue to inject drugs.

claims.claim: For acute hepatitis, test for HCV PCR 6 months after the possible infection date as the patient may have cleared the infection, and speak to a specialist if the patient is unwell
claims.source_text: Acute hepatitis Test for HCV PCR 6 months after possible infection date - the patient may have cleared the infection. Speak to a specialist if the patient is unwell

claims.claim: For chronic infection all positive patients should be treated
claims.source_text: Chronic infection All positive patients should be treated

claims.claim: Referral to a specialist is recommended if complications such as cirrhosis are suspected, and the Hepatitis C Consensus Statement states all people with cirrhosis should be referred to and managed in consultation with a specialist familiar with the management of this condition
claims.source_text: Complications Referral to specialist if complications suspected e.g. cirrhosis. The Hepatitis C Consensus Statement states: All people with cirrhosis should be referred to, and managed in consultation with, a specialist familiar with the management of this condition

claims.claim: An alternative for complications is to commence treatment and send the patient to a specialist or speak to a specialist
claims.source_text: Commence treatment and send the patient to a specialist or speak to a specialist.

claims.claim: Upper limits of normal ALT are 30 IU/L for male sex and 19 IU/L for female sex, with AST 40 for the APRI calculator
claims.source_text: Liver function test (LFT) Upper limits of normal ALT - male sex 30 IU/L; female sex 19 IU/L, AST 40/L for APRI calculator

claims.claim: The platelet count from a full blood count is important for the APRI score, and an APRI above 1 indicates increased likelihood of cirrhosis
claims.source_text: Full blood count Platelet count important for APRI score ... APRI Above 1: increased likelihood of cirrhosis

claims.claim: Increasing AFP levels may indicate hepatocellular carcinoma, the upper limit of normal is 10 or below, and AFP may be elevated in other conditions
claims.source_text: AFP Increasing levels may indicate Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Upper limit of normal ≤ 10 May be elevated in other conditions

claims.claim: HCV genotype is not required for treatment but is recommended as part of clinical assessment where possible
claims.source_text: HCV genotype Viral subtype: not required for treatment but is recommended as part of clinical assessment where possible

claims.claim: HCV resistance testing is done by a specialist to guide treatment if initial treatment has failed
claims.source_text: HCV resistance testing Done by a specialist to guide treatment if initial treatment has failed

claims.claim: The MBS schedule should be checked for pre-treatment, on-treatment and post-treatment item numbers and testing amounts per 12-month periods
claims.source_text: Medicare Benefits Schedule (MBS): check the schedule for pre-treatment, on-treatment and post-treatment item number and testing amounts per 12-month periods

claims.claim: Vaccinate for hepatitis A and B if susceptible, and screen for STIs and other blood borne viruses including HIV and syphilis
claims.source_text: Vaccinate for hepatitis A and B, if susceptible. - Screen for sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and other blood borne viruses (HIV and syphilis

claims.claim: Notify the state or territory health department if required, only if HCV PCR is detected
claims.source_text: Notify the state/territory health department if required (only if HCV PCR detected).

claims.claim: All babies of HCV RNA positive women should be tested with an HCV PCR test at 8 weeks of age and then 4-6 weeks later, and if positive the baby will need specialist management
claims.source_text: All babies of HCV RNA positive women should be tested with an HCV PCR test at 8 weeks of age and then 4-6 weeks later. If positive, the baby will need specialist management.

claims.claim: Treatment with DAA is available for HCV PCR positive children from 12 years of age and older
claims.source_text: Treatment for HCV PCR positive children from ≥ 12 years old with DAA

claims.claim: Past failed treatment or current treatment failure should be referred to a specialist, and co-infection with HIV or HBV should be referred to specialist services
claims.source_text: Past failed treatment or current treatment failure (positive SVR) Refer to a specialist ... Co-infection with HIV, HBV Refer to specialist services

claims.claim: Test of cure is an HCV PCR at 4 weeks after completion of treatment; if negative counsel about possible risk behaviour and re-infection, and if positive retest at 12 weeks post treatment
claims.source_text: TOC-HCV PCR at 4 weeks after completion of treatment, if negative, counsel about possible risk behaviour and re-infection; if positive, retest at 12 weeks post treatment.

claims.claim: Sustained viral response is defined as test of cure 12 weeks after the completion of treatment
claims.source_text: SVR- Sustained Viral Response (TOC 12 weeks after the completion of treatment)

claims.claim: Patients with chronic hepatitis C should be assessed for other causes of hepatitis such as alcohol and fatty liver and counselled to reduce these factors if relevant
claims.source_text: Patients with chronic hepatitis C should be assessed for other causes of hepatitis (e.g. alcohol, fatty liver), and should be counselled to reduce these factors if relevant (e.g. reduced alcohol intake)

claims.claim: Populations at risk include people with current or a history of injecting drug use, previous incarceration, birth in HCV endemic countries and regions, receipt of blood products before 1990 or in developing countries, condomless anal sex with a partner with HCV infection, participation in group sex, and current HIV PrEP use
claims.source_text: Populations at risk include: people with current or history of injecting drug use; previous incarceration; born in hepatitis C virus (HCV) endemic countries and regions; received blood products before 1990 or in developing countries; engage in condomless anal sex with a partner with HCV infection, participate in group sex and current HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) use

claims.claim: About 75% of people with hepatitis C infection will progress to chronic hepatitis
claims.source_text: About 75% of people with hepatitis C infection will progress to chronic hepatitis.

claims.claim: Asymptomatic hepatitis C infection is common and acute hepatitis is uncommon
claims.source_text: Asymptomatic infection: common - Acute hepatitis: uncommon

claims.claim: Chronic HCV is defined as an HCV viral load detected in the absence of clinical features of acute hepatitis infection
claims.source_text: Chronic HCV is defined as a HCV VL detected in the absence of clinical features of acute hepatitis infection.

claims.claim: Disease progression is usually slow but may cause cirrhosis, liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma, and is affected by age at infection, duration of infection, alcohol and other drug use, co-infection with HIV or HBV, male gender, stage of fibrosis, higher ALT levels and other comorbid conditions such as diabetes
claims.source_text: Disease progression is usually slow but may cause cirrhosis, liver failure and hepatocellular carcinoma. - Disease progression can be affected by age at infection, duration of infection, alcohol and other drug use, co-infection with HIV or hepatitis B virus (HBV), male gender, stage of fibrosis and higher alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels, other comorbid conditions e.g. diabetes

claims.claim: Hepatitis C is low risk for sexual exposure and contact tracing is not generally performed for sexual partners, while contacts via parenteral exposure such as shared needles or injecting equipment should be tested if possible
claims.source_text: Low risk for sexual exposure, contact tracing not generally performed for sexual partners - Contacts via parenteral exposure (shared needles, injecting equipment) should be tested if possible

claims.claim: Children of mothers who are HCV PCR positive and not tested in the post-natal period should be tested
claims.source_text: Children of mothers who are HCV PCR positive and not tested in the post-natal period should be tested.

claims.claim: Hepatitis C is caused by infection with the single-stranded RNA hepatitis C virus
claims.source_text: Infection with the single-stranded RNA hepatitis C virus.
